TX.name: Texas

authority.name: Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation
aliases: Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation
authority.source_quote: TDLR regulates elevators, escalators and related equipment to ensure the safety of passengers. TDLR also regulates contractors and inspectors who work with elevators, escalators, and other related equipment.

statute.citation: Texas Health and Safety Code Chapter 754
statute.source_quote: HEALTH AND SAFETY CODE CHAPTER 754. ELEVATORS, ESCALATORS, AND RELATED EQUIPMENT

rules.source_quote: The Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation (Department) is reviewing the Elevators, Escalators, and Related Equipment rules located at Title 16, Texas Administrative Code, Chapter 74 for re-adoption, revision, or repeal.

code_adoption.existing_installations: ASME A17.3-2002 continues in effect (16 TAC §74.100); Health and Safety Code §754.014(d) requires all equipment, regardless of installation date, to meet ASME A17.3.
amendments_detail: Deletes requirement 1.2.1(c) and all references to ASME A17.7.
Deletes 2.12.7.2.1(c), hoistway access switch on sight guard.
Deletes 7.4.2.2 and all references to Type B material lifts.
Deletes 8.6.4.19.7 and 8.6.5.14.3(f), standby or emergency power operation.
Deletes 8.10.2.2.1(q), emergency or standby power operation.
Deletes 8.10.2.3.2(l) and 8.10.3.3.2(l), emergency or standby power alterations.
Deletes the reference to ASME A17.3 contained within 9.1.
Deletes Appendix E in its entirety.
code_adoption.source_note: Official SOS TAC viewer is JavaScript-only; rule text via Cornell LII, corroborated by TDLR's plan-review page (https://www.tdlr.texas.gov/elevator/plan-review.htm) citing ASME A17.1-2016.
code_adoption.source_quote: (1) ASME Code A17.1-2016/CSA B44-16 as amended in subsection (b); ... (1) ASME Code A17.1-2016/CSA B44-16 and the amendments in subsection (b) shall be effective on November 1, 2018.

requirements.claim: Texas building owners must have elevators, escalators and related equipment inspected annually by a TDLR-registered elevator inspector.
requirements.source_quote: (1) have the equipment inspected annually by a registered elevator inspector, unless the equipment has been removed from service in accordance with commission rules;

requirements.claim: Texas elevator inspectors register with TDLR but are not TDLR employees.
requirements.source_quote: Elevator inspectors are required to register with the Department, but they are not employees of the Department.

requirements.claim: In Texas, the building owner has the sole right to select the elevator inspector.
requirements.source_quote: The owner has the sole right to select the inspector who enters upon the property.

requirements.claim: A Texas registered elevator inspector must give the owner the inspection report within five calendar days of the inspection.
requirements.source_quote: A registered elevator inspector shall issue an inspection report to the owner not later than the fifth calendar day after the date of inspection

requirements.claim: Texas building owners must obtain a TDLR Certificate of Compliance for each unit of equipment, and the certificate is valid for one year.
requirements.source_quote: The owner of the building is responsible for obtaining a Certificate of Compliance for each unit of equipment in the building. This certificate is good for one year and must be applied for annually.

requirements.claim: Texas owners must display the Certificate of Compliance in a publicly visible area of the building.
requirements.source_quote: (4) display the certificate of compliance for the equipment in a publicly visible area as defined by commission rule; and

requirements.claim: Texas owners must have cited violations corrected or under contract to be corrected within 30 days of the inspection, or obtain a waiver or delay from TDLR.
requirements.source_quote: The Building’s owner is responsible for having cited violations corrected, or under contract to be corrected, within 30 days of the date of inspection, or must obtain a Waiver or Delay from the Department.

requirements.claim: Texas owners must report each accident involving elevator equipment to TDLR within 24 hours.
requirements.source_quote: (e) An owner shall report to the department each accident involving equipment not later than 24 hours following the accident.

requirements.claim: In Texas, a person may not install, repair, alter, test or maintain elevator equipment without registering as a contractor with TDLR.
requirements.source_quote: A person may not install, repair, alter, test, or maintain equipment without registering as a contractor with the department as required by this chapter.

requirements.claim: Under Texas law, the term contractor does not include an employee of a contractor.
requirements.source_quote: "Contractor" means a person engaged in the installation, alteration, testing, repair, or maintenance of equipment. The term does not include an employee of a contractor

requirements.claim: Texas elevator contractor and inspector registrations expire one year after they are issued.
requirements.source_quote: A registration expires on the first anniversary of the date of issuance.

requirements.claim: Texas elevator contractors must carry general liability insurance of at least $1,000,000 per occurrence for bodily injury or death and $500,000 per occurrence for property damage.
requirements.source_quote: The required general liability insurance must be not less than: $1,000,000 for each single occurrence of bodily injury or death and; $500,000 for each single occurrence of property damage.

requirements.claim: Each Texas elevator contractor must designate one or two responsible parties with at least three years of elevator contractor experience.
requirements.source_quote: (a) Each contractor who registers with the department must designate at least one but not more than two responsible parties. ... (1) have a minimum of three years of elevator contractor experience related to elevator installation, repair, and maintenance;

requirements.claim: Before installing an elevator or escalator in Texas, the registered contractor must submit plans to TDLR and obtain approval.
requirements.source_quote: Before installing an elevator or escalator, the registered elevator contractor must submit detailed plans to TDLR and obtain approval of the plans.

requirements.claim: Texas requires a Category 5 full-load test every five years on electric (traction) elevators.
requirements.source_quote: Every five years, a Category 5, full-load test must be performed. Category 5 testing is required only on Electric (a.k.a. traction) elevators

requirements.claim: In Texas, a passenger elevator without working door restrictors must be removed from service immediately.
requirements.source_quote: For safety reasons, any passenger elevator in Texas without Door Restrictors OR found to have non-working Door Restrictors must be immediately removed from service.

requirements.claim: In Texas, a passenger elevator without firefighters' service or with non-working Phase One firefighters' service must be removed from service immediately.
requirements.source_quote: In order to protect the public, any passenger elevator in Texas without Firefighters’ Service OR found to have non-working Phase One Firefighters’ Service must be immediately removed from service.

requirements.claim: The Texas elevator law does not apply to equipment in buildings owned and operated by the federal government.
requirements.source_quote: (c) This chapter does not apply to equipment located in a building owned and operated by the federal government.

requirements.claim: TDLR does not regulate elevators in single-family dwellings, except that state law requires an inspection by a TDLR-registered inspector after installation.
requirements.source_quote: Equipment installed in single-family dwellings is not regulated by TDLR except for provisions in Section 754.0141 that require an inspection by a registered TDLR inspector after it is installed.

local_authorities.name: City of Houston
local_authorities.scope: TDLR does not regulate elevators or escalators inside Houston city limits; the City of Houston runs its own program. Its adopted code edition and rules are not verified — do not state them, and never say TDLR inspects or permits elevators in Houston.
local_authorities.source_quote: TDLR does not regulate elevators or escalators located inside the City of Houston city limits.

not_the_regulator.name: Texas Department of Insurance
not_the_regulator.why: TDI regulates insurance, runs workers' compensation and houses the State Fire Marshal's Office; it does not run the Texas elevator program.
not_the_regulator.source_quote: The Texas Department of Insurance regulates the state’s insurance industry, oversees the administration of the Texas workers’ compensation system, performs the duties of the State Fire Marshal’s Office

wrong_citations.wrong: Texas Administrative Code Title 28 (Insurance) for elevator rules

not_required.claim: TDLR's adopted state elevator code is ASME A17.1-2016; never present video or two-way text messaging as a Texas elevator requirement.
not_required.why: Houston runs its own program and cities can adopt newer building codes, so never claim either way that they are not required anywhere in Texas.
not_required.source_quote: (1) ASME Code A17.1-2016/CSA B44-16 as amended in subsection (b);

CA.name: California

authority.name: Division of Occupational Safety and Health (Cal/OSHA)
authority.program: Elevator Unit, California Department of Industrial Relations
aliases: Division of Occupational Safety and Health
authority.source_quote: Mission of the Cal/OSHA Elevator Unit: To ensure the safety of the riding public and protect workers in the elevator industry, the Elevator Unit will maintain a vigilant system to meet our obligation to inspect and enforce code compliance for elevators and other conveyances.

statute.source_quote: CHAPTER 2. Elevators, Escalators, Platform and Stairway Chair Lifts, Dumbwaiters, Moving Walks, Automated People Movers, and Other Conveyances [7300 - 7324.2]

rules.citation: California Code of Regulations, Title 8, Elevator Safety Orders (Sections 3000–3146)
rules.source_quote: Subchapter 6. Elevator Safety Orders ... GROUP 4. CONVEYANCE INSTALLATIONS FOR WHICH THE INSTALLATION CONTRACT WAS SIGNED ON OR AFTER MAY 1, 2008

code_adoption.effective: May 1, 2008, for installation contracts signed on or after that date
code_adoption.existing_installations: Older installations fall under Group II and Group III of the Elevator Safety Orders.
amendments_detail: Where the Elevator Safety Orders differ from ASME A17.1-2004, the Elevator Safety Orders apply (8 CCR §3140(b)(4)).
code_adoption.source_quote: Conveyances covered by ASME A17.1-2004, section 1.1, Scope, and Article 41 of Title 8 shall comply with ASME A17.1-2004, Safety Code for Elevators and Escalators, except sections 1.1.3, 2.2.2.5, 2.7.6, 2.11.1.2, 2.11.1.4, 2.12.6, 2.14.2.2(f), and 2.14.2.6

requirements.claim: No elevator may be operated in California without a valid, current permit to operate issued by Cal/OSHA.
requirements.source_quote: No elevator shall be operated without a valid, current permit issued by the Division.

requirements.claim: In California, the permit to operate for a passenger, freight or inclined elevator must be posted conspicuously in the elevator car.
requirements.source_quote: The permit, or a copy thereof, to operate a passenger elevator, freight elevator or incline elevator shall be posted conspicuously and securely in the elevator car.

requirements.claim: California law requires every conveyance to be inspected at least once a year, and a conveyance found safe receives a permit to operate for up to one year.
requirements.source_quote: (a) Except as provided in subdivision (b), the division shall cause all conveyances to be inspected at least once each year. If a conveyance is found upon inspection to be in a safe condition for operation, a permit for operation for not longer than one year shall be issued by the division.

requirements.claim: Cal/OSHA may issue a permit to operate for up to two years for an elevator in safe condition that is covered by a full maintenance contract with a C-11 licensed elevator company.
requirements.source_quote: will be covered during the entire term of the permit by a full maintenance contract with an elevator service company possessing a C-11 license issued by the California Contractors' State License Board, the Division may issue a permit for a period not exceeding two years.

requirements.claim: In California, arranging the annual reinspection is the elevator owner's responsibility.
requirements.source_quote: Annual Inspections (Reinspections) Are the Responsibility of the Elevator Owner

requirements.claim: Only State of California safety engineers and Certified Competent Conveyance Inspectors (CCCI) may perform elevator inspections in California.
requirements.source_quote: Only Safety Engineers employed by the State of California and Certified Competent Conveyance Inspectors (CCCI) are authorized to perform inspections in California.

requirements.claim: In California, each new elevator must be inspected by Cal/OSHA and receive a permit to operate before it is placed in service.
requirements.source_quote: (1) Each new device shall be inspected by an authorized representative of the Division and a permit to operate issued before the device is placed in service.

requirements.claim: In California, a permit from Cal/OSHA is required before a conveyance is erected, installed or materially altered.
requirements.source_quote: no conveyance may be erected, constructed, installed, or materially altered, as defined by regulation of the division, unless a permit has been obtained from the division before the work is commenced.

requirements.claim: Companies that install, alter, test, maintain, repair or service elevators in California must be certified by Cal/OSHA as a Certified Qualified Conveyance Company (CQCC).
requirements.source_quote: no conveyance subject to this chapter shall be erected, constructed, installed, materially altered, tested, maintained, repaired, or serviced by any person, firm, or corporation unless the person, firm, or corporation is certified by the division as a certified qualified conveyance company.

requirements.claim: Applicants for CQCC certification in California must submit a current C-11 contractor license and certificates of workers' compensation and liability insurance.
requirements.source_quote: Submit a copy of a current and valid C-11 license ... Submit a copy of current Workers' Compensation insurance certificate ... Submit a copy of current Liability insurance certificate

requirements.claim: The California Contractors State License Board (CSLB) issues the C-11 Elevator Contractor license; permits to operate, inspections and CQCC/CCCM certification are Cal/OSHA's.
requirements.source_quote: C-11 - Elevator Contractor ... An elevator contractor fabricates, erects, installs and repairs elevators

requirements.claim: Anyone who works on an elevator in California without supervision must be certified by Cal/OSHA as a Certified Competent Conveyance Mechanic (CCCM).
requirements.source_quote: any person who, without supervision, erects, constructs, installs, alters, tests, maintains, services or repairs, removes, or dismantles any conveyance covered by this chapter, shall be certified as a certified competent conveyance mechanic by the division.

requirements.claim: In California, only a Certified Competent Conveyance Mechanic working for a Certified Qualified Conveyance Company may maintain, repair, alter or replace components on a conveyance.
requirements.source_quote: only a Certified Competent Conveyance Mechanic working for a Certified Qualified Conveyance Company is authorized to perform any maintenance, repairs, alterations, or replacements on any conveyance subject to those orders.

requirements.claim: California CQCC, CCCM and conveyance inspector certificates last two years, and renewal requires at least eight hours of continuing education.
requirements.source_quote: shall have a term of two years ... This continuing education course shall consist of not less than eight hours of instruction

requirements.claim: California's elevator law exempts conveyances under federal jurisdiction and conveyances in single-unit private homes that are not accessible to the public.
requirements.source_quote: (1) Conveyances under the jurisdiction of the United States government. (2) Conveyances located in a single-unit private home and not accessible to the public.

requirements.claim: California has proposed a Group V update to its Elevator Safety Orders that would incorporate ASME A17.1-2019 in part; the Standards Board held the public hearing on June 18, 2026, and no effective date has been posted.
requirements.source_quote: Elevator Safety Orders - Group V ELEVATOR SAFETY ORDERS, Subchapter 6 Status Public hearing: Jun. 18, 2026 ... Filed with Secretary of State: Effective date: Rulemaking Documents

local_authorities.name: City of Los Angeles, Department of Building and Safety (LADBS)
local_authorities.scope: Los Angeles runs its own elevator and conveyance inspection program (per a 2018 City Controller audit; current details not re-verified). Say only that Los Angeles has its own program.
local_authorities.source_quote: The City of Los Angeles is unique in that no other local jurisdiction within the State has it own elevator and conveyance inspection program.

unverified: Video / text-based emergency communication: UNSETTLED. Group IV adopts A17.1-2004, but the 2025 California Building Code §3001.2 (effective 2026-01-01) appears to require visual and audible two-way communication; final text and scope not fetched. Never claim California does NOT require it.
Los Angeles program: only a 2018 audit could be fetched (LADBS blocks automated fetches).
ASME A17.3 for existing installations: referenced in the Labor Code but no incorporating Elevator Safety Orders section found.
cautions: Whether California requires visual or text-based elevator emergency communication is unsettled: the Elevator Safety Orders adopt ASME A17.1-2004, but the 2025 California Building Code appears to add visual and audible two-way communication (not verified). Never claim California does or does not require it.

MD.name: Maryland

authority.name: Maryland Department of Labor, Division of Labor and Industry
authority.program: Elevator and Escalator Safety (Safety Inspection Unit); mechanics and contractors are licensed by the Maryland Elevator Safety Review Board
authority.source_quote: Division of Labor and Industry Elevator and Escalator Safety 10946 Golden West Drive, Suite 160 Hunt Valley, MD 21031.

statute.citation: Annotated Code of Maryland, Public Safety Article, Title 12, Subtitle 8 (§§ 12-801 to 12-842)
statute.source_quote: Elevator Safety Law Public Safety Article, Title 12, Subtitle 8, Annotated Code of Maryland

rules.source_quote: Chapter 81 Elevator, Escalator, and Chairlift Safety

code_adoption.edition: 2022 edition (ASME A17.1-2022/CSA B44:22), with Maryland changes; the edition that applies depends on when the installation contract was signed

Requirements in effect at a unit's first certification stay in effect, and units installed before July 1, 1955 may keep operating without being rebuilt to the current Safety Code, with some exceptions (see requirements initial_certification_requirements_remain and pre_1955_units).

code_adoption.source_quote: ASME A17.1 2022: Safety Code for Elevators, Escalators, Moving Walks, and Dumbwaiters Adopted 6/17/2026

requirements.claim: In Maryland, an elevator unit may not be operated unless the Commissioner of Labor and Industry has issued a certificate for it.
requirements.source_quote: (a) An elevator unit may not be operated in a building, structure, or place of employment in the State unless a certificate is issued by the Commissioner.

requirements.claim: The certificate must be posted conspicuously in or on the elevator unit.
requirements.source_quote: (b) The certificate shall be posted conspicuously in or on the elevator unit.

requirements.claim: Each elevator unit in Maryland must have a periodic annual inspection by a State inspector or a third-party qualified elevator inspector.
requirements.source_quote: (b) (1) Except as provided in paragraph (2) of this subsection, each elevator unit in the State shall have a periodic annual inspection by a State inspector as provided for in § 12–809(a)(6) of this subtitle or by a third–party qualified elevator inspector

requirements.claim: The owner must hire a third-party qualified elevator inspector to conduct the periodic inspections required by the Safety Code.
requirements.source_quote: (d) (1) An owner shall hire a third–party qualified elevator inspector to conduct all periodic inspections that are required by the Safety Code.

requirements.claim: The State conducts a final acceptance inspection after an elevator unit is installed, modified, or altered and before it is placed in service.
requirements.source_quote: The Commissioner shall conduct a final acceptance inspection on completion of the installation, modification, or alteration of an elevator unit before it is placed in service.

requirements.claim: Tests performed for a required inspection must be performed by a licensed elevator mechanic.
requirements.source_quote: (d) (1) A test on an elevator unit performed in connection with an inspection required by this subtitle, the Safety Code, or a regulation adopted by the Commissioner shall be performed by a licensed elevator mechanic.

requirements.claim: When a third-party qualified elevator inspector is required to witness a test, the inspector must be physically present for the entire test.
requirements.source_quote: (2) A third–party qualified elevator inspector required to witness a test performed on an elevator unit in accordance with this subtitle, the Safety Code, or a regulation adopted by the Commissioner shall be physically present during the entire test

requirements.claim: Owners must ensure that elevators suspended by wire ropes, belts, chains, or similar means, and rack and pinion elevators, receive a comprehensive five-year inspection.
requirements.source_quote: D. An owner shall ensure that an elevator unit suspended by wire ropes, belts, chains, or a similar suspension or an elevator with rack and pinion drive has a comprehensive 5-year inspection.

requirements.claim: Each elevator unit must be registered with the Commissioner at least 60 days before its planned completion and before it is placed in service.
requirements.source_quote: (a) Except as otherwise provided in this section, each elevator unit owned or to be operated shall be registered with the Commissioner at least 60 days before its planned completion and before it is placed in service.

requirements.claim: Owners must re-register their elevator units with the Commissioner every year, at the time of the periodic annual inspection.
requirements.source_quote: State law requires that the owner re-register their elevator units with the Commissioner annually. The annual re-registration will coincide with the periodic annual inspection.

requirements.claim: A person must be licensed by the Maryland Elevator Safety Review Board as an elevator mechanic before working on elevator units in Maryland.
requirements.source_quote: (a) Except as otherwise provided in Part III of this subtitle, a person shall be licensed by the Board as an elevator mechanic before the person erects, constructs, wires, alters, replaces, maintains, repairs, dismantles, or services elevator units in the State.

requirements.claim: A business must be licensed by the Board as an elevator contractor before engaging in the business of installing, altering, maintaining, repairing, or servicing elevator units in Maryland.
requirements.source_quote: (b) Except as otherwise provided in Part III of this subtitle, a person shall be licensed by the Board as an elevator contractor before the person engages in the business of erecting, constructing, wiring, altering, replacing, maintaining, repairing, dismantling, or servicing

requirements.claim: Elevator contractors must carry at least $1,000,000 in general liability insurance and at least $500,000 in property damage insurance.
requirements.source_quote: covered by: (1) general liability insurance in the amount of at least $1,000,000; and (2) property damage insurance in the amount of at least $500,000.

requirements.claim: The Maryland Elevator Safety Review Board, within the Maryland Department of Labor, licenses and regulates elevator mechanics and contractors.
requirements.source_quote: The Maryland Elevator Safety Review Board licenses and regulates individuals who engage in the business of erecting, constructing, wiring, altering, replacing, maintaining, repairing, dismantling, or servicing elevators, dumbwaiters, escalators, and moving walks.

requirements.claim: Maintenance, repair, test, and inspection records must be kept at a readily accessible central location in the building where the elevator is located.
requirements.source_quote: A. Record Keeping. At a readily accessible central location in the building where the elevator unit is located, a contractor, owner, or lessee shall maintain:

requirements.claim: In Maryland, the safety code edition that applies to a new elevator depends on the date the installation contract is signed.
requirements.source_quote: (2) The applicable adopted safety code will be contingent upon the date the contract to install an elevator unit is signed.

requirements.claim: Before adopting the 2022 edition, Maryland adopted ASME A17.1-2019/CSA B44-19 (COMAR 09.12.81.01DD), effective October 22, 2022.
requirements.source_quote: Regulation .01DD adopted effective October 22, 2022 (49:9 Md. R. 531)

requirements.claim: Requirements in effect when an elevator was first certified remain in effect for that elevator.
requirements.source_quote: (5) Requirements prescribed at the time of the initial elevator certification remain in effect.

requirements.claim: Elevators installed before July 1, 1955, may be used without being rebuilt to the current Safety Code, but each elevator must still have standard hoistway entrance protection.
requirements.source_quote: an elevator unit installed before July 1, 1955, may be used without being altered or rebuilt to comply with the requirements of the Safety Code. (ii) Each elevator shall be equipped with standard hoistway entrance protection

requirements.claim: Maryland's elevator inspection and certificate law generally does not apply to units in privately owned single-family homes or in buildings under federal control.
requirements.source_quote: (a) (1) Part II of this subtitle does not apply to an elevator unit that is: (i) except as provided in paragraphs (2) and (3) of this subsection, installed in a privately owned single–family residential dwelling; or (ii) installed in a building or structure under federal control or regulation.

requirements.claim: Each new Maryland building constructed after July 1, 1985, with at least one planned elevator must have a passenger elevator that can carry a 6-foot-8-inch rescue litter horizontally.
requirements.source_quote: (b) Each new building constructed after July 1, 1985, in which at least one elevator is planned, shall have a passenger elevator that can accommodate a horizontally carried and positioned 6 foot 8 inch rescue litter.

not_the_regulator.name: Maryland Department of Labor, Licensing and Regulation
aliases: Maryland Department of Labor, Licensing, and Regulation
not_the_regulator.why: Former name — renamed the Maryland Department of Labor in 2019. Use the current name.
not_the_regulator.source_quote: Renaming the Department of Labor, Licensing, and Regulation to be the Maryland Department of Labor

unverified: Text-based and video emergency communication: Maryland adopted ASME A17.1-2019/CSA B44-19 (effective Oct 22, 2022) and ASME A17.1-2022/CSA B44:22 (effective June 17, 2026). None of Maryland's changes to the 2022 edition touch Section 2.27, so no 'not required' entry is recorded. No official Maryland page describes what Section 2.27 requires, so the exact communication requirements were not confirmed from a state source.

Local elevator programs: Public Safety § 12-807(b) directs the Commissioner to accept certificates of inspection from a political subdivision or municipal corporation. No official source was found showing that any Maryland county or city (including Baltimore City) currently runs its own elevator certificate program.

ASME A17.3 (existing installations): no reference to A17.3 was found in COMAR 09.12.81.01 or on the Department's code page. That it is not adopted is inferred from its absence, not stated by the State.
The Department's elevator law page also lists COMAR 09.12.61, which regs.maryland.gov titles 'Amusement Attractions'. It does not appear to be an elevator chapter and is left out.

DC.name: District of Columbia

authority.name: District of Columbia Department of Buildings
authority.program: Elevator and conveyance inspections and certificates (inspections by DOB-approved third-party agencies)
authority.source_quote: Effective October 1, 2025, the Department of Buildings (DOB) has oversight for inspections and certifications of conveyances.

statute.citation: D.C. Official Code § 6-1409 (Construction Codes Approval and Amendments Act of 1986)
statute.source_quote: The Mayor may issue rules to amend the Construction Codes and to adopt new supplements and editions of the Model Codes in whole or in part pursuant to subchapter I of Chapter 5 of Title 2.

rules.source_quote: The District of Columbia Building Code (2017), referred to as the “Building Code,” consists of the 2015 edition of the International Building Code (International Building Code), published by the International Code Council (ICC), as amended by the Building Code Supplement of 2017 (12-A DCMR).

code_adoption.edition: 2013 edition (ASME A17.1-2013/CSA B44-13), as referenced by the 2017 DC Building Code with District amendments

authority.program: Bureau of Occupational and Industrial Safety, Elevator Section (statewide, including Philadelphia)

statute.source_quote: The provisions of this Chapter 405 issued under sections 105(c) and 301 of the Pennsylvania Construction Code Act (35 P.S. § § 7210.105(c) and 7210.301), unless otherwise noted.

requirements.claim: In Pennsylvania, an elevator may not be operated unless the Department of Labor and Industry has issued a certificate of operation for it.
requirements.source_quote: (a) An elevator or lifting device may not be operated unless the Department issues a certificate of operation for the designated classification of the elevator or other lifting device.

requirements.claim: For equipment with a machine room, the certificate of operation or a copy must be posted in the elevator car or attached to the controller in the machine room.
requirements.source_quote: (d) The certificate of operation or a copy of the certificate of operation for equipment with a machine room shall be posted in the elevator car or other lifting device enclosure, or attached to the controller in the machine room.

requirements.claim: A certificate of operation is valid for 24 months for equipment on a 6-month inspection cycle and 48 months for equipment on a 12-month cycle.

requirements.claim: Electric elevators, hydraulic elevators, and escalators in Pennsylvania must have periodic inspections at intervals of no more than 6 months.

requirements.claim: Any UCC-certified elevator inspector may conduct a periodic inspection in Pennsylvania.

requirements.claim: The Department conducts an acceptance inspection before a new, repaired, altered, or modified elevator is put into service.

requirements.claim: After a major repair, replacement, or alteration, an elevator may not return to service until the Department inspects and passes it.

requirements.claim: Starting December 20, 2026, Category 1 tests must be performed every year as a stand-alone requirement; previously they were done together with the 3-year and 5-year tests.
requirements.source_quote: the department and ESB determine that Category 1 testing should be performed annually as a stand-alone requirement to ensure additional safety

requirements.claim: In Florida, once a certificate of operation is issued, the elevator owner is responsible for safe operation, proper maintenance, inspection, and correction of code deficiencies.
requirements.source_quote: The elevator owner is responsible for the safe operation, proper maintenance, and inspection and correction of code deficiencies of the elevator after a certificate of operation has been issued by the department.

requirements.claim: Florida registered elevator companies must register with the state every year and maintain general liability insurance.
requirements.source_quote: Each registered elevator company must annually register with the division and maintain general liability insurance coverage in the minimum amounts set by rule.

requirements.claim: All new conveyance installations in Florida must be performed by a registered elevator company.
requirements.source_quote: All new conveyance installations must be performed by a registered elevator company.

requirements.claim: In Florida, a certified elevator technician is authorized to construct, install, maintain or repair conveyances after the state issues them an elevator certificate of competency.
requirements.source_quote: "Certified elevator technician" means a natural person authorized by the division to construct, install, maintain, or repair any vertical conveyance, after having been issued an elevator certificate of competency by the division.

requirements.claim: Florida certified elevator technicians must register with the state every year and carry general liability insurance.
requirements.source_quote: Each certified elevator technician must annually register with the division and be covered by general liability insurance coverage in the minimum amounts set by the division.

requirements.claim: A Florida elevator certificate of competency expires after 1 year and is renewed with proof of 8 hours of continuing education.
requirements.source_quote: Such credential shall be valid for and expire at the end of 1 year, and may be renewed by the division when the division receives proof of the elevator certificate of competency holder's completion of 8 hours of continuing education

requirements.claim: Florida certified elevator inspectors must keep their qualified elevator inspector credential in good standing.
requirements.source_quote: Failure by a certified elevator inspector to maintain his or her qualified elevator inspector credential in good standing.

requirements.claim: Florida certified elevator inspectors must register with the state every year and show 8 hours of continuing education, good standing, and general liability insurance.
requirements.source_quote: Each certified elevator inspector must annually register with the division and provide proof of completion of 8 hours of continuing education, proof of good standing, and proof of general liability insurance coverage

requirements.claim: In Florida, the certificate of operation holder must report any elevator accident to the state within 5 working days.
requirements.source_quote: Within 5 working days after any accident occurring in or upon any elevator, the certificate of operation holder shall report the accident to the division on a form prescribed by the division.

requirements.claim: Elevators, stairway chairlifts and wheelchair lifts in private residences do not need a Florida certificate of operation.
requirements.source_quote: Vertical conveyances, including stairway chairlifts, and inclined or vertical wheelchair lifts located in private residences are not required to obtain a certificate of operation under this chapter.

local_authorities.name: Broward County Building Code Division
local_authorities.scope: Enforces Florida's elevator law (Chapter 399) through its own elevator inspectors in Broward County, which includes Pompano Beach; the page does not list the cities covered.
local_authorities.source_quote: Mandates in Chapter 399 of the Florida State Statutes regarding elevator safety are monitored and strictly enforced by Broward County Building Code elevator inspectors.

local_authorities.name: Miami-Dade County Office of Elevator Safety
local_authorities.scope: Covers all Miami-Dade municipalities except the City of Miami and the City of Miami Beach, which run their own elevator offices.
local_authorities.source_quote: located within buildings throughout Miami-Dade County as regulated by the State of Florida Statutes Chapter 399, the Florida Building Code Chapter 30, and Florida Administrative Code 61c-5 in all municipalities, except the City of Miami and City of Miami Beach.

local_authorities.name: City of Miami Beach Elevator Safety Division
local_authorities.scope: Holds delegated authority under s. 399.13 for elevator permits, inspections and certificates in Miami Beach.
local_authorities.source_quote: Under Florida Statutes, Elevator Safety Act, Chapter 399, Rule 399.13, The Elevator Safety Division has been delegated the Jurisdictional Authority over elevators, escalators, moving walks, wheelchair lifts and related equipment in the City of Miami Beach.

local_authorities.name: City of Miami Building Department Elevator Division
local_authorities.scope: Reviews annual inspection reports and issues the Annual Elevator Certificate in the City of Miami.
local_authorities.source_quote: The Building Department Elevator Division will review your Elevator Inspection Report. If the inspection passed, you will receive your Elevator Certificate via mail to the address listed under the customer account.

AZ.name: Arizona

authority.name: Industrial Commission of Arizona (ICA), Elevator Division
authority.program: Elevator Division (called the ADOSH Elevator Safety Section until September 12, 2026)
authority.source_quote: "Division" means the elevator division of the commission.

statute.citation: A.R.S. §§ 23-491 through 23-491.16 (Safety Conditions for Elevators and Similar Conveyances), as amended by Laws 2026, Ch. 73
statute.source_quote: The commission shall: 1. Administer this article through the division.

rules.citation: Arizona Administrative Code R20-5-502 through R20-5-515 (Elevator and Conveyance Safety)
rules.source_quote: R20-5-507 - Safety Code for Elevators, Escalators, Dumbwaiters, Moving Walks, Material Lifts, Special Purpose Personnel Elevators, and Dumbwaiters with Automatic Transfer Devices

code_adoption.edition: 2019 edition (ASME A17.1-2019), for equipment installed, repaired or altered on or after January 1, 2023
code_adoption.existing_installations: No ASME A17.3 adoption found; older equipment may comply with the edition in effect at installation.
amendments_detail: For repairs or alterations, compliance applies to the extent possible to the scope of the work.
Later amendments or editions of ASME A17.1 are not incorporated.
code_adoption.source_quote: installed, repaired, or altered on or after January 1, 2023, shall comply with the ASME A17.1-2019 (Safety Code for Elevators and Escalators) or ASME A17.7-2007 (Performance-Based Safety Code for Elevators and Escalators) as referenced in ASME A17.1-2019, which are incorporated by reference.

requirements.claim: Arizona owners must have each conveyance inspected before it first goes into service, after any modification or alteration, and annually after that.
requirements.source_quote: (a) Before placing a conveyance in operation after the initial installation of the conveyance. (b) After modification or alteration of a conveyance. (c) After the inspection pursuant to subdivision (a), annually or as otherwise directed by the commission.

requirements.claim: No conveyance may operate in Arizona without an annual certificate of inspection issued by the state.
requirements.source_quote: No conveyance shall be operated in this state without an annual certificate of inspection issued by the division.

requirements.claim: In Arizona, the owner must keep the state certificate at the same location as the conveyance and make it available for inspection on request.
requirements.source_quote: The owner or operator of a conveyance shall maintain the Commission's certificate at the same location as the conveyance or related equipment and make the certificate available for inspection and copying upon request.

requirements.claim: In Arizona, the state serial number or the certificate must be posted in or close to the conveyance in an easily accessible location.
requirements.source_quote: The State Serial Number or certificate shall be posted or displayed in or within close proximity to the conveyance in a location that is easily accessible.

requirements.claim: Arizona owners may hire a private elevator inspector authorized by the Industrial Commission of Arizona to perform initial or annual inspections.
requirements.source_quote: The commission shall compile a list of private elevator inspectors that are currently authorized pursuant to subsection A. An owner or an operator may hire a private elevator inspector.

requirements.claim: Arizona private elevator inspectors must register with the commission every year and show at least eight hours of approved continuing education.
requirements.source_quote: A private elevator inspector shall register with the commission annually and provide proof of all of the following with the registration: 1. Completion of at least eight hours of continuing education approved by the commission.

requirements.claim: An Arizona private elevator inspector may not inspect a conveyance owned, operated or last serviced by the inspector, a company the inspector owns, or the inspector's employer.
requirements.source_quote: Inspect a conveyance owned, operated or last serviced by any of the following: (a) The private elevator inspector. (b) A company owned by the private elevator inspector. (c) A company for which the private elevator inspector is an employee at the time of the inspection.

requirements.claim: In Arizona, using a private elevator inspector does not relieve the owner or operator of their legal obligations.
requirements.source_quote: An owner or operator is not relieved of the obligations under this article by the use of a private elevator inspector.

requirements.claim: Arizona owners must notify the state at least 90 days before installing, relocating, or altering a conveyance.
requirements.source_quote: The owner or operator of a conveyance shall notify the Elevator Safety Section at least 90 days before installation, relocation, or alteration of a conveyance.

requirements.claim: Arizona owners must notify the state within 24 hours of any accident that injures a person or disables a conveyance.
requirements.source_quote: The owner or operator of a conveyance shall notify the Elevator Safety Section within 24 hours of every accident resulting in injury to a person or disabling damage to a conveyance.

requirements.claim: Every Arizona conveyance is assigned a state serial number on a tag fixed to the controller or mainline disconnect.
requirements.source_quote: The Elevator Safety Section shall assign a State Serial Number to every conveyance for recordkeeping purposes. The State Serial Number shall be on a tag that is affixed to the controller or mainline disconnect of the conveyance.

requirements.claim: Arizona conveyances with firefighters' emergency operation must use the Arizona Firefighters Service (AZFS) key.
requirements.source_quote: All conveyances equipped with firefighters' emergency operation shall utilize the AZFS key.

requirements.claim: In Arizona, lawfully installed older conveyances may stay in use unless the state's elevator chief considers the use a hazard to life, health or property.
requirements.source_quote: Existing conveyances lawfully installed before the effective date of this article may continue in use if the use is, in the opinion of the chief, not a hazard to life, health or property.

requirements.claim: Arizona platform lifts and stairway chairlifts installed, repaired, or altered on or after January 1, 2023 must comply with ASME A18.1-2020.
requirements.source_quote: Every owner or operator of a platform lift or stairway chairlift installed, repaired, or altered on or after January 1, 2023, shall comply with ASME A18.1-2020 (Safety Standard for Platform Lifts and Stairway Chairlifts)

requirements.claim: The Arizona Registrar of Contractors has R-12 and C-12 elevator license classifications that allow the licensee to install and repair elevators, dumbwaiters, escalators, and moving walks.
requirements.source_quote: The Elevators Classification R-12 and C-12 allows the licensee to install and repair elevators, dumbwaiters, escalators, moving walks and ramps and stage and orchestra lifts.

local_authorities.name: City of Phoenix Elevator Section (Planning and Development Department)
local_authorities.scope: Inspects elevators, escalators, moving walks, dumbwaiters and chair lifts inside the City of Phoenix; the state handles equipment outside Phoenix.
local_authorities.source_quote: The City of Phoenix Elevator Section inspects elevators, escalators, moving walks, dumbwaiters and chair lifts located within Phoenix's jurisdiction.

SC.name: South Carolina

authority.name: South Carolina Department of Labor, Licensing and Regulation (LLR), Office of Elevators and Amusement Rides
authority.program: Office of Elevators and Amusement Rides
aliases: South Carolina Department of Labor, Licensing and Regulation
SC LLR Office of Elevators and Amusement Rides
authority.source_quote: The South Carolina Department of Labor, Licensing and Regulation, Office of Elevators and Amusement Rides, proposes to amend its regulations, appearing in Chapter 71 of the South Carolina Code of Regulations

statute.citation: S.C. Code Title 41, Chapter 16 (South Carolina Elevator Code)
statute.source_quote: This chapter is known and may be cited as the "South Carolina Elevator Code".

rules.citation: S.C. Code of Regulations Chapter 71, Article 5 (Safety Standards for Elevator Facilities), Regulations 71-5000 through 71-5700
rules.source_quote: ARTICLE 5 SAFETY STANDARDS FOR ELEVATOR FACILITIES 71-5000. Purpose and Definitions.

code_adoption.edition: 2019 edition (ASME A17.1-2019/CSA B44:19), adopted without amendment
code_adoption.effective: adopted by notice in the S.C. State Register on July 23, 2021
code_adoption.existing_installations: Facilities in operation before July 1, 1986 follow the 1986 edition of ANSI A17.3.
code_adoption.source_quote: the Department of Labor, Licensing and Regulation hereby adopts the latest edition of the following nationally recognized code as set forth herein below: 1. Safety Code for Elevators and Escalators, (ASME) A17.1-2019/CSA B44:19, 2019 edition.

requirements.claim: South Carolina requires elevators to be inspected at installation, registration, alteration or repair, and at least once a year after that before the operating certificate is renewed.
requirements.source_quote: shall be inspected upon initial installation or registration, or at the time of alteration or repair prior to issuing an operating certificate and a minimum of one (1) time per year thereafter, prior to renewing an operating certificate.

requirements.claim: In South Carolina, handicap lifts are inspected every five years; manlifts, television tower elevators and special purpose elevators every seven years; dumbwaiters when installed or altered.
requirements.source_quote: b) Dumbwaiters shall be inspected each time they are installed or altered. c) Handicap lifts shall be inspected every five (5) years. d) Manlifts, television tower elevators and special purpose elevators shall be inspected every seven (7) years.

requirements.claim: In South Carolina, required inspections may be made only by state inspectors or special inspectors, and a special inspector's inspection may be accepted in place of a state inspection.
requirements.source_quote: The inspections required by items 1 to 3 of this section must be made only by inspectors or special inspectors. An inspection by a special inspector may be accepted by the Director in lieu of a required inspection by an inspector.

requirements.claim: In South Carolina, no elevator facility may be operated without a certificate of registration and an operating certificate from the state.
requirements.source_quote: A person, firm, or corporation shall not operate any facility serving any building or structure without a certificate of registration and an operating certificate issued by the Director.

requirements.claim: In South Carolina, the operating certificate, or a copy, must be displayed conspicuously inside each elevator car.
requirements.source_quote: An operating certificate shall be displayed in a conspicuous location within each elevator car, or on a permanent object adjacent to all other types of facilities. In the alternative, a facsimile copy of the original operating certificate may be posted within each elevator car

requirements.claim: In South Carolina, a state construction permit is required before any elevator facility is erected, constructed, altered or installed.
requirements.source_quote: A person, firm or corporation shall not erect, construct, alter or install after July 1, 1986, any facility without first obtaining from the Director a construction permit for such work.

requirements.claim: South Carolina special inspectors must be licensed and show the qualifications in the 2018 edition of QEI-1, the American National Standard for Qualification of Elevator Inspectors.
requirements.source_quote: Any applicant for a license as a special inspector shall present evidence of all qualifications as stated in the 2018 edition of QEI-1, The American National Standard for Qualification of Elevator Inspectors

requirements.claim: In South Carolina, a special inspector may not inspect an elevator on which the inspector or the inspector's employer has a current service or warranty contract.
requirements.source_quote: It is unlawful for a special inspector to perform elevator inspections under this chapter or regulations promulgated pursuant to it on an elevator on which he or his employer has a current service or warranty contract.

requirements.claim: In South Carolina, the owner must keep every elevator facility in safe operating condition and in line with state regulations.
requirements.source_quote: Every facility must be maintained by the owner in a safe operating condition and in conformity with the regulations promulgated by the Director.

requirements.claim: In South Carolina, an accident that seriously injures anyone other than an employee must be reported to the state before the end of the next working day.
requirements.source_quote: is involved in an accident which results in a serious injury to any person other than an employee shall report the injury to the Director before the end of the next working day.

requirements.claim: The South Carolina Elevator Code does not apply to equipment in a single private dwelling.
requirements.source_quote: The provisions of this chapter do not apply to any facility installed in any single private dwelling residence or to facilities over which an agency of the federal government is asserting similar enforcement jurisdiction.

requirements.claim: Local ordinances that conflict with the South Carolina Elevator Code or its regulations are void.
requirements.source_quote: Any ordinance, bylaw, or resolution relating to the inspection, construction, installation, alteration, maintenance, or operation of facilities within the limits of the political subdivision, which conflicts with this chapter or with regulations promulgated by the Director, is void.

requirements.claim: In South Carolina, new elevator facilities must comply with the officially adopted edition of ASME A17.1 in effect when the permit is issued.
requirements.source_quote: All facilities installed after July 1, 1986, shall comply with the officially adopted editions of the ASME A17.1 Elevator Code and all supplements thereto, at the time the permit is issued.

requirements.claim: South Carolina elevator facilities in operation before July 1, 1986 must comply with the 1986 edition of ANSI A17.3, the safety code for existing elevators and escalators.
requirements.source_quote: All facilities for which construction or relocation was begun or which were in operation prior to July 1, 1986, in South Carolina shall comply with the requirements of the 1986 edition of the ANSI A17.3, the American National Standard Safety Code for Existing Elevators and Escalators.

requirements.claim: In South Carolina, newly installed underground hydraulic elevator cylinders must be encased in plastic outer containment to limit electrolytic corrosion.
requirements.source_quote: All newly installed underground hydraulic pressure cylinders shall be encased in an outer plastic containment to minimize electrolytic corrosion.

requirements.claim: In South Carolina, firefighters' service on new installations must use the five-pin S.C. #1000 key.
requirements.source_quote: The key switches required to operate firefighters' service on Phase I and II shall use a five pin key, S.C. #1000.

requirements.claim: South Carolina passenger elevators must have standby power that runs emergency lighting and the alarm bell for at least four hours if normal power fails.
requirements.source_quote: All passenger elevators shall be equipped with a standby power source capable of operating emergency lighting and the alarm bell for a period of at least four (4) hours in the event the normal power source fails.
